name: Jasaaï
title: One of the sons of Bani who divorced his foreign wife
summary: Jasaaï was an Israelite from the lineage of Bani who lived in the period after the Babylonian exile. He was among the men who had taken foreign wives and, at Ezra's command, agreed to divorce them to preserve the religious purity of the people. His name is mentioned in the list of those who repented in the book of Ezra.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's reforms against mixed marriages
keyEvents.description: Ezra discovered that many Israelites, including priests and Levites, had married women from surrounding nations, which was contrary to God's law.

keyEvents.title: The people's confession and pledge
keyEvents.description: The people gathered, confessed their sin of intermarriage, and pledged to separate from their foreign wives.

keyEvents.title: Investigative commission established
keyEvents.description: A commission was appointed to investigate who had taken foreign wives, and all were instructed to appear within three days.

keyEvents.title: Jasaaï mentioned among the sons of Bani
keyEvents.description: Jasaaï is listed among the sons of Bani who had married foreign women and agreed to send them away.

keyEvents.title: List of those who divorced their wives
keyEvents.description: A complete list was kept of all the men from various families who committed themselves to divorcing their foreign wives, as a sign of repentance and faithfulness to the covenant.
